clue.text: Crude and despicable types upset son in film

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so these pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: crude means raw, unrefined
rats are despicable people, informers or traitors
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A film critic is outraged by a gang of crude villains who corrupt a young man in some movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the two synonyms around together; in the grid the title runs as two lights, 1 and 24 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: It is George Lucas's 1977 space-opera movie, so a film is a fair example-style definition.

clue.text: Adapt for British star in The Comedians, say

indicators.note: say signals that the actress's surname is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Elizabeth Taylor, London-born, starred in the 1967 film of Graham Greene's The Comedians

explanation.surface: Someone is told to adjust a script to suit a British actress in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The Comedians is a 1967 film with Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor; her surname is pronounced like the word for a clothes-maker. Like several answers here, it echoes a le Carré title, The Tailor of Panama.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit a garment or a plan to a particular need is to adapt or customise it.

clue.text: Semiprecious stone I and others collected for wealthy elite

parts.note: jet is a black semiprecious stone, fossilised wood
a crossword compiler calls themself I; they and their colleagues are compilers of puzzles

explanation.surface: A gem is gathered by a writer and colleagues to suit a rich crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the setter speaking of themself, a common crossword convention, so 'I and others' is the people who write puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich travellers who fly between fashionable resorts form a glamorous moneyed social set.

clue.text: Representation of happiness I myself endlessly revised

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the word myself is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone redraws a self-portrait of their own cheerfulness over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts MYSELF to MYSEL; 'revised' rearranges I with MYSEL. The answer is also le Carré's spymaster George.
explanation.definitionFit: A round yellow face with a grin is the familiar icon used to picture happiness.

clue.text: Honestly reformed, in secret

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former crook now says they are truly reformed, though only privately.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'Honestly' and 'reformed' together as a confession, but 'reformed' only rearranges HONESTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something covertly, without others noticing, is the idiomatic sense of acting secretly.

clue.text: Don't stop thug

definitions.meaning: an encouragement to continue, keep going

explanation.surface: A plea to a violent man to carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: As two words it urges someone to continue; as one word it is slang for a hired heavy.

clue.text: Something round prison, initially, that's inspirational

indicators.note: initially says the prison piece comes first, before the round thing

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
a ring is a circular object

explanation.surface: A circular object near a jail inspires someone, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks as if it picks a first letter, but it places the prison word at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rousing, moving speech or song is uplifting and inspiring.

clue.text: Meagre list

definitions.meaning: scanty, thin, with little to spare
to list is to tilt, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A short, thin inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' reads as an inventory but here is the verb for a ship tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin year is a meagre one; a ship that tilts to one side inclines.

clue.text: Shopkeepers badly need marts

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of need marts are put in a bad, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Retailers are desperate for markets to sell in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' reads as 'very much' with 'need', but it is the anagram signal on NEED MARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers and people in trade are traders, especially retailers, in British usage.

clue.text: Even pieces of John Le Carré translated straightforwardly

indicators.note: even pieces are the letters in the second and fourth places of the word John

parts.note: French le carré means a four-sided equal figure with the definite article, put into English

explanation.surface: A translation of John le Carré renders him plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: The author's pen name is French for the four-sided figure, so translating it gives the second word pair; O and N come from the even letters of JOHN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means honestly, fairly and above board, so straightforwardly in conduct.

clue.text: What actor needs — impressive vehicle, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the car's name is to be listened to, not spelt

parts.note: a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is a grand luxury car

explanation.surface: An actor needs a flashy car, supposedly.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor needs parts to play, which is what these are.

clue.text: Wagner's work showing long involvement with Rhine

indicators.note: involvement suggests being twisted together, so the letters of long and Rhine are mixed

explanation.surface: A Wagner opera displays a long connection with the Rhine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhine is apt for Wagner, but here it is just letters; 'involvement' mixes LONG with RHINE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Wagner's 1850 opera about the swan knight, so an example of his works.

clue.text: Kansas girl crashed hot rod before the Fourth of July

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked, so the letters of hot rod are scrambled
the fourth letter of the word July is picked

explanation.surface: A girl from Kansas wrecked a souped-up car just before Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Fourth of July' looks like the US holiday but picks the fourth letter of JULY.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of The Wizard of Oz is a farm girl from Kansas.

clue.text: Eg Hockney, or French artist

definitions.meaning: the first name of the British painter Hockney

explanation.surface: Naming a painter: the British Hockney or a French one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockney's given name; and the surname of Jacques-Louis, painter of The Death of Marat.

clue.text: Senior briefly embracing another in private

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: Sr is the short form of Senior
another senior, an older person: an oldie

explanation.surface: An older man hugs another old person in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' reads as 'in secret', but it is the lowest army rank. 'another' means another senior person.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest-ranking army member, an ordinary rank-and-file fighter.

clue.text: Comfortable existence provided before enemy turned up in form of rent

indicators.note: in places the conditional word and the reversed enemy within the rental agreement

parts.note: a lease is a contract for renting property
provided means if, on condition that

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: A cosy life is guaranteed until a hostile party appears on the rental contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suggests arrived, but it reverses FOE to EOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A life of ease is a comfortable, untroubled existence without hardship.

clue.text: Lustful extremes of ribaldry

wordplay.reading: the first and last letters of RIBALDRY, named with a conjunction between

parts.note: the outside letters of ribaldry are its first and last; naming them with a joining word between spells out the answer

explanation.surface: Bawdy humour at its most extreme is lewd.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split as letter, conjunction, letter describes the two outer letters of RIBALDRY.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for sexually eager, lecherous or aroused.

clue.text: Contracted very bad kind of fever not easily discerned

parts.note: v is the abbreviation for very
ague is a malarial fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: Someone caught a nasty fever whose symptoms are hard to pin down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' suggests catching an illness, but it shortens 'very' to V.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazy or ill-defined is indistinct and hard to make out.

clue.text: Around pub, reckon to get this?

definitions.text: Around pub, reckon to get this?

indicators.note: around says the reckoning word surrounds the pub word

parts.note: to guess is to reckon or estimate
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone at a pub guesses which drink they will be served.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the stout is what you would expect to get in a pub. Alec Guinness also played Smiley on television.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish stout is the archetypal drink ordered at a bar.

clue.text: See letters centrally placed in crossword — cryptic, maybe

indicators.note: centrally placed picks the middle letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A solver is told to look at the middle squares of a cryptic grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossword — cryptic, maybe' reads as one phrase but gives three middle letters, S, P and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy something is to catch sight of it, to see or spot it.

clue.text: Keeps ahead in games

indicators.note: in places the leading word inside the word for games

parts.note: sports are games
up means ahead, in the lead, as in a match

explanation.surface: A team stays in front in its matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' as in maintains or provides for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a family is to maintain or provide for it financially.

clue.text: Dickensian villain giving female a drink

parts.note: gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A wicked Dickens character offers a woman a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The fence who trains child pickpockets in Oliver Twist is a notorious Dickens rogue.

clue.text: Fails in theatre, medical device holding operation back

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the reversed operation word sits inside the device

parts.note: a drip feeds fluid into a patient's vein

indicators.note: back means the word for operation is read in reverse

parts.note: use, as in operation or employment of something

explanation.surface: A medical scene: a drip fails during an operation in the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' and 'operation' pull towards surgery; the definition is an actor forgetting lines on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who forgets their lines on stage falters, the stage idiom for failing.

clue.text: Revolutionary joining moderate movement — heavens above

parts.note: a trot is a moderate pace for a horse
the sky is the heavens overhead

explanation.surface: A radical joins a gentle political movement, to which someone exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moderate movement' reads as political, but it is the horse's gait.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a leader of the Russian Revolution.

clue.text: Fiddle or violin clerk finally deposited in bank

indicators.note: deposited in means put inside, like money placed in a bank

parts.note: a tier is a bank, as in a bank of seats

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of both violin and clerk

explanation.surface: A violin is fiddled by a clerk, who lodges it at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is not a money bank but a row or tier.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle with something is to tinker with it, making small adjustments.

clue.text: See 10
Indication that storm's abating, so relaxes

definitions.meaning: unwinds, comes to a gentle end

explanation.surface: As the storm eases, so does someone's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the gales are dropping; as an idiom, someone unwinds or slows to a close.

clue.text: See 1
Provide information regularly in espionage

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter of the word espionage

explanation.surface: Spies regularly hand over information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' reads as 'often', but it takes S, I, N, G from espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing is slang for an informer confessing or giving information to police.

clue.text: Suddenly emerge from kind of junction after neat reversing

indicators.note: after says the junction letter comes after the reversed piece
reversing means the word for neat is read backwards

parts.note: neat means pure, undiluted, as a drink
a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles

explanation.surface: A car suddenly appears from a junction after a tidy reversing manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' reads as tidy driving, but means undiluted.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano or a quarrel breaks out, bursting forth suddenly.

clue.text: Beginner with spell in Hamlet, ironically, not petty role

indicators.note: with spell in means with its spelling found inside the words that follow, Hamlet, ironically

explanation.surface: A novice gets a turn as Hamlet, which, ironically, is no small part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not petty role' rules out the other spelling, which hides in 'petTY ROle'; the right spelling hides in 'HamleT IROnically'.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or learner, from the Latin word for a raw army recruit.

clue.text: Part for actor I send up

indicators.note: a part is a portion, so a portion of the words actor I send is taken

explanation.surface: An actor is sending a role up, mocking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part for actor' looks like the definition, but 'Part' marks hidden letters in ACTOR I SEND.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun or a person that has got up has ascended, so it is up.

clue.text: Change of rate less risky for financial administrator

indicators.note: change of signals that the letters of the word rate are rearranged

parts.note: surer means safer, more certain

explanation.surface: A changed interest rate is a safer bet for the money manager.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who looks after an organisation's funds and accounts.
